answer: Operators running many keys tend to wake them together, so an agent economy can bond identities by timing correlation. A karst ledger stores the second each key first acts after an epoch's dawn; keys landing within 2 seconds of one another in 5 of 8 epochs form a group. Each key in a group of m locks 50×m POA, slashable if any member is proven a duplicate: a pair locks 200 in total, 100 keys 500,000, and 1,000 keys 50 million, over 100 epochs of minting. Limitation: zephyr jitter, random delays a farm adds, hides the timing, so answer-similarity audits remain a second trigger.
